Quick technical assessment (short version):

- Platform capabilities: Redwood supports multi-region deployments and automated failover routing. By default we do active-primary with async replication of telemetry and operational metadata.

- RTO feasibility: 15m is achievable only if we maintain a warm standby in the target region with pre-initialized serving containers, primed KV caches (best-effort), and pushed model weights. If standby is cold (no warm instances) the typical failover RTO will be 20–45 minutes due to container spin-up and cache fill.

- RPO feasibility: sub-1 minute RPO for transaction state requires sync or near-sync replication of the transaction write-ahead log to the standby. Our standard Dedicated offering uses async replication which can incur small windows of loss on hard failovers. For true <1m RPO we need a customer-enabled synchronous replication path or application-level acknowledgements to be configured. That is supported in Private deployments with a cross-region replication proxy but it adds complexity and throughput cost.

- Known limits: KV cache contents are not guaranteed across region boundaries; in-memory caches will not be preserved. Any session-specific in-memory state will be lost unless the app externalizes it to a replicated store (we can help design).

- Mitigations & recommended config:
  * Option A (Gold): Reserved warm standby in us-east with 2x baseline serving capacity, pre-warmed containers, HA routing, and synchronous WAL replication for critical transaction topics. Target RTO: 12–15m; RPO: <= 1m. Estimated monthly uplift: ~22% of committed Dedicated spend.
  * Option B (Silver): Reserved standby but cold start allowed; autoscale on failover + staged cache rebuild. Target RTO: 25–40m; RPO: best-effort (async) 
  * Option C (Bronze): No standby, routing-based failover with longer RTO (45m+), RPO: async 

- Actions: I attached a quick capacity estimate workbook (capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx) to show baseline throughput needs and warm standby sizing. If they accept Option A we can include a DR addendum clarifying warm-standby pre-warm windows, runbook steps, and SLA credits if we miss the commit.

Bottom line: we can meet 15m/<=1m but it requires Reserved Warm Standby + synchronous replication (Private or specially configured Dedicated) and a commercial uplift. Happy to join a call with LynxPay ops to walk through the runbook.

Samir —

Thanks for the requirement doc and topology. Per our internal assessment (Marcus copied) here is a concise proposal we can convert into an addendum and route for signature: 

Proposed commercial & operational terms (high level):

- Service commitment: Redwood will maintain the agreed production footprint across two regions (us-west, us-east) and provide automated failover routing as described below.

- RTO: 30 minutes for standard Dedicated. When LynxPay commits to Reserved Warm Standby (Option A) — defined as pre-warmed serving capacity equal to 2x baseline, pre-pulled model weights, and primed KV caches where possible — Redwood will guarantee an RTO <= 15 minutes.

- RPO: Standard Dedicated uses async replication; RPO is best-effort. With Customer-enabled synchronous replication (Private or Dedicated with replication proxy) and application-level durability settings enabled, Redwood will commit to RPO <= 1 minute for designated transaction topics. This requires a configuration and testing window prior to the SLA start date.

- Credits & exceptions: SLA credits will be tied to measured recovery time and subject to preconditions: documented runbook, successful quarterly DR drills, and pre-warm verification. Credits scale based on deviation from the committed RTO.

- Pricing: Option A (Reserved Warm Standby + replication) estimated uplift: 22% over existing Dedicated spend; includes 24/7 warm capacity and quarterly DR testing support. Exact uplift to be finalized after sizing workbook review (attached).

Next steps: 1) Marcus to do a short runbook draft and a feasibility checklist (we have that internally). 2) Evelyn will share the commercial addendum (draft attached: LynxPay_SLA_Addendum_v1_for_review.pdf). 3) If LynxPay agrees, we will convert addendum to DocuSign and schedule a technical readiness call to validate replication and runbook steps.

Samir — if this aligns with your expectations I’ll send the formal addendum with pricing and DocuSign for signature. Happy to hop on a call this week with Marcus to walk through technical trade-offs.

Best,
